weakPassword.label: Weak Passwords
weakPassword.description: A password is weak when the space an attacker has to search is small: it is short, it draws on a narrow set of characters, or it is built from a word, name or keyboard run that sits in every cracking dictionary. Offline guessing runs at billions of attempts per second, so anything in that class falls quickly. Replace it with a long, randomly generated one.

reusedPassword.label: Reused Passwords
reusedPassword.description: One password used in several places means a single breach anywhere unlocks all of them — and you have no say in which of those services will be the one to leak. Give every item its own generated password so a leak stays contained to the account it came from.

compromisedPassword.label: Compromised Passwords
compromisedPassword.description: This password appears in a public record of breached credentials, which puts it on the lists attackers try first no matter how strong it looks. Change it everywhere it is used: a password only has to leak once to stay leaked.

faq.title: Questions
faq.subtitle: Answers to common questions
faq.forgetQ: What if I forget my secret?
faq.forgetA1: Your vault cannot be recovered — not by you, not by us. The key is made from your secret alone, so without it the file stays unreadable. That is the cost of nobody else being able to read it either.
faq.forgetA2: What you can do is start over: $forgot on the unlock screen sets up a new, empty vault. Your old file is not deleted — it is renamed to $file and kept in your keeperpass folder, so the data is still there if the secret comes back.
faq.forgetA3: Write your secret down and keep it somewhere safe. It is the one thing in KeeperPass that cannot be replaced.
faq.seeA: No — and not as a promise, as a consequence of the design. Encryption happens on this phone and the ciphertext goes straight to your own storage. There is no KeeperPass server in the path to see anything.
faq.syncA: Yes. Every device reads the same file from your storage. Sign in with the same account, enter the same secret, and your vault is there.
faq.providerQ: What if my storage provider reads the file?
faq.providerA: They would see encrypted bytes. The key never leaves this phone, so Google, Dropbox or any other provider cannot read the contents.
faq.importQ: Can I import from another password manager?
faq.importA: Yes — export to CSV there, then use Import in Settings.
faq.changeSecretQ: How do I change my secret?
faq.changeSecretA: Open Settings and choose $action. You enter your current secret and the new one; your vault is decrypted, re-encrypted under the new secret, and saved back. Nothing is lost — every item comes with you, and the change applies on every device the next time it loads your vault.
faq.costA: Nothing. KeeperPass is free and open-source, and it stores data in cloud space you already have.
faq.contactBody: Questions, feedback or a problem to report? Send us an email.
